messages.text: 我想先了解一下大概流程。Hunyuan3D 2.0 是怎么从一张输入图片生成 3D shape 的？能不能先简单讲讲这个 shape generation 的主要步骤，我后面再看细节。

messages.short_answer: 简单说，Hunyuan3D 2.0 的 shape 部分分两步：先用 Hunyuan3D-ShapeVAE 把 3D 网格压缩成潜空间中的一串连续 token；再用基于 flow 的扩散 Transformer（Hunyuan3D-DiT）在这个潜空间里，根据输入图片预测 token 序列，最后由 VAE 解码器把 token 解码成多边形网格。

sections.title: 流程的三个主要环节
sections.text: 论文说 shape 生成模型由两部分组成：一是把 polygon mesh 压缩成潜空间连续 token 的自编码器，二是在该潜空间上训练、以用户图片为条件预测 token 序列的扩散模型；预测出的 token 再经 VAE 解码器还原为网格。论文同时指出，给定输入图片后，Hunyuan3D-DiT 先生成 bare mesh，之后才进入纹理生成阶段。

sections.title: 用通俗的话理解这条流程
sections.text: 可以把它理解为：先学一个“压缩字典”（ShapeVAE），能把一个 3D 形状压成少量潜变量并再还原；然后学一个“按图作画”的生成器（DiT），在这些潜变量中，根据输入图片生成合适的潜变量；最后用字典把潜变量还原成网格。这种做法借鉴了图像和视频生成中成功的潜扩散模型思路。

sections.title: 论文中的关键设计
sections.text: 论文称 shape 生成采用潜扩散模型的架构，并说明这一设计受到潜扩散模型在图像和视频生成中成功应用的启发。在训练上，DiT 是在 ShapeVAE 的潜空间上，用 flow-matching 目标训练的 dual-single stream transformer。

sections.title: 对你的研究的参考价值
sections.text: 如果你的目标是从网络照片生成 AR 可用的 3D 资产，这条“单图 → 潜空间 token → 网格”的路线可以作为一个参考基线：它把形状生成与输入图片条件解耦，并且在潜空间里做扩散。你可以先思考：网络照片通常有遮挡、光照和背景干扰，而论文的 DiT 输入是用户提供的图片，这一点需要你自己判断是否适合你的数据。

sources.text: This design is driven by the successful applications of latent diffusion models in image and video generation. Specifically, our shape generation model consists of (1) an autoencoder – Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE (Sec. 3.1) that compresses the shape of a 3D asset represented by polygon mesh into a sequence of continuous tokens in the latent space; (2) a flow-based diffusion model – Hunyuan3D-DiT (Sec. 3.2), trained on the latent space of ShapeV AE for predicting object token sequences from a user-provided image. The predicted tokens are further decoded into a polygon mesh with V AE decoder. The details of these models are illustrated below. 3.1 Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE employs vector sets, a compact neural representation for 3D shapes proposed by 3DShape2VecSet [112], which has also been leveraged in the recent work Dora [11]. Followed by Michelangelo [119], we use a variational encoder-decoder transformer for shape compression and decoding.
quotes: The predicted tokens are further decoded into a polygon mesh with V AE decoder.

sources.text: The comparison shows the superiority of Hunyuan3D 2.0 in alignment between conditional images and generated meshes, generation of fine-grained details, and human preference ratings. 2 Hunyuan3D 2.0 Architecture In this section, we elaborate on the model architecture of Hunyuan3D 2.0, focusing on two main components: the shape generation model and the texture generation model. Fig. 2 illustrates the pipeline of Hunyuan3D 2.0 for creating a high-resolution textured 3D asset. Given an input image, Hunyuan3D-DiT initially generates a high-fidelity bare mesh via the shape generation model. This model comprises a Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE and a Hunyuan3D-DiT, which will be discussed in Sec. 3. Subsequently, by leveraging strong geometric priors and the input image, we introduce Hunyuan3D- Paint as our texture generation model in Sec. 4. This model produces self-consistent multi-view outputs, which are used for baking high-definition texture maps.

sources.text: To this end, we presentHunyuan3D 2.0, a 3D asset creation system with two strong open-sourced 3D foundation models:Hunyuan3D-DiTfor generative shape creation andHunyuan3D-Paintfor generative texture synthesis. Hunyuan3D 2.0 features a two-stage generation pipeline, starting with the creation of a bare mesh, followed by the synthesis of a texture map for that mesh. This strategy is effective for decoupling the difficulties of shape and texture generation [ 34, 107, 46, 47] and also provides flexibility for texturing either generated or handcrafted meshes. With this architecture, our shape creation model – Hunyuan3D-DiT, is designed as a large-scale flow-based diffusion model. As a prerequisite, we first train an autoencoder – Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE using advanced techniques such as mesh surface importance sampling and variational token length to capture fine-grained details on the meshes. Then, we build up a dual-single stream transformer [ 45] on the latent space of our V AE with the flow-matching [53, 24] objective.
quotes: Then, we build up a dual-single stream transformer [ 45] on the latent space of our V AE with the flow-matching [53, 24] objective.

messages.text: 好，流程我大概懂了。所以 Hunyuan3D-DiT 在同一步里就把颜色和纹理也一起生成了，对吧？那你刚才说的那三个环节，最后解码出来的网格已经是带贴图的了，我下一步直接拿来用就行？

messages.short_answer: 不是。根据论文，Hunyuan3D-DiT 只生成无纹理的裸网格（bare mesh），颜色和纹理由单独的 Hunyuan3D-Paint 模型在第二阶段生成。所以你刚才理解的三个环节解码出来的是几何网格，还不是带贴图的模型。

sections.title: 两阶段流程的分工
sections.text: 论文说 Hunyuan3D 2.0 采用两阶段生成流程：先生成裸网格，再为该网格合成纹理贴图。作者认为这种策略有助于分开处理形状和纹理生成的难点。

sections.title: 纹理阶段的输入与输出
sections.text: 论文中 Hunyuan3D-Paint 以生成网格的法线图和位置图作为几何条件，输出用于烘焙的多视角图像，再烘焙成高清纹理贴图。这说明纹理依赖已生成的几何。

sections.title: 对你的 AR 研究的参考价值
sections.text: 如果你的目标是从网络照片生成 AR 可用的 3D 资产，可以把 DiT 看作几何生成部分，把 Paint 看作可单独替换或补充的纹理部分。是否直接采用 Paint，或者改用其他纹理方法，需要你根据自己的数据和 AR 平台要求决定。

messages.short_answer: 可以这样理解：Hunyuan3D-DiT 只负责根据输入图片生成无纹理的几何网格（裸网格）；Hunyuan3D-Paint 则以这个网格的法线图和位置图为几何条件，并结合输入图片，生成多视角图像，再烘焙成纹理贴图。两者的衔接点就是 DiT 输出的网格。

sections.title: 两阶段的分工
sections.text: 论文说 Hunyuan3D 2.0 采用两阶段流程：先生成裸网格，再为该网格合成纹理图。DiT 是几何生成模型，Paint 是纹理生成模型，这种分工用于解耦形状和纹理生成的难度。

sections.title: 输入输出如何衔接
sections.text: DiT 的输入是一张图片，输出是裸网格。Paint 的输入包括 DiT 生成网格的法线图和位置图（几何条件），论文还提到它利用输入图片；输出是用于烘焙的多视角图像，最终得到高分辨率纹理贴图。下面的“渲染得到法线图和位置图”这一步是我的推断，论文原文没有逐步展开。

sections.title: 对你的 AR 研究的参考价值
sections.text: 由于纹理阶段可以作用于生成的网格，也可以作用于手工制作的网格，如果你的 AR 资产需要替换或保留某一部分（例如只用几何或只做纹理），这种模块化结构可能值得参考。是否采用、如何采用，需要你根据自己的数据和目标来判断。

messages.short_answer: 根据目前检索到的段落，论文只说明 Hunyuan3D-DiT 以一张输入图片为条件生成裸网格，但没有说明它对图片的背景、光照或遮挡有什么具体要求。Image Delighting 确实是为光照和阴影服务的，但它属于纹理阶段（Hunyuan3D-Paint）的预处理，目的是防止光照被烘焙进贴图，并不是 DiT 的输入处理，也不直接处理杂乱背景或遮挡。

sections.title: DiT 的输入条件：论文说了什么
sections.text: 论文只写到 Hunyuan3D-DiT 根据给定的输入图片生成高保真的裸网格，没有在这些段落里列出对单张图、背景干净程度或遮挡的要求。因此，“输入必须是单张干净图片”这一点在现有段落中无法确认。

sections.title: Image Delighting 解决的是纹理阶段的光照问题
sections.text: 论文指出，用户收集或 T2I 模型生成的参考图通常有明显且多变的光照和阴影，直接输入多视角生成框架会让光照和阴影被烘焙进纹理贴图。因此 Image Delighting 是在多视角生成之前对输入图做的处理，服务于纹理。这一段描述的是 Paint 部分，而不是 DiT 的输入。

sources.text: To achieve these objectives, we employ a three-stage framework, including a pre-processing stage (Sec. 4.1), a multi-view image synthesis stage (Sec. 4.2, Hunyuan3D-Paint), and a texture baking stage based on dense multi-view inference (Sec. 4.3). Other details related to model training and textand image-to-texture pipeline are provided in Sec. 4.4. Fig. 5 illustrates the complete pipeline of our texture map synthesis method. 4.1 Pre-processing Image Delighting Module.The reference image typically exhibits pronounced and varied illumination and shadow, whether collected by the user or generated by T2I models. Directly inputting such images into the multi-view generation framework can cause illumination and shadows to be baked into the texture maps. To address this issue, we leverage a delighting procedure on the input image via an image-to-image approach [6] before multi-view generation. Specifically, to train such an image delighting model, we collect a large-scale 3D dataset and render it under the illumination of a random HDRI environmental map and an even white light to form the corresponding pair-wise image data.
quotes: The reference image typically exhibits pronounced and varied illumination and shadow, whether collected by the user or generated by T2I models. Directly inputting such images into the multi-view generation framework can cause illumination and shadows to be baked into the texture maps.

sources.text: These pages describe the Hunyuan3D-DiT shape generation transformer, which uses double- and single-stream blocks to let shape latent tokens and image condition tokens interact, with timestep-only modulation and no positional embedding on the latent sequence. Image conditioning uses DINOv2 Giant features at 518x518 with background removal and centering, and training follows a flow matching objective with an affine conditional optimal transport path and Euler ODE sampling at inference. The pages then introduce Hunyuan3D-Paint, a generative texture map synthesis pipeline with image delighting as pre-processing, a reference-net and multi-task attention for multi-view consistency, and a geometry-aware greedy viewpoint selection strategy using 8 to 12 views. Details of the multi-view synthesis and texture baking stages are only referenced, not fully described on these pages.

To achieve these objectives, we employ a three-stage framework, including a pre-processing stage (Sec. 4.1), a multi-view image synthesis stage (Sec. 4.2, Hunyuan3D-Paint), and a texture baking stage based on dense multi-view inference (Sec. 4.3). Other details related to model training and textand image-to-texture pipeline are provided in Sec. 4.4. Fig. 5 illustrates the complete pipeline of our texture map synthesis method. 4.1 Pre-processing Image Delighting Module.The reference image typically exhibits pronounced and varied illumination and shadow, whether collected by the user or generated by T2I models. Directly inputting such images into the multi-view generation framework can cause illumination and shadows to be baked into the texture maps. To address this issue, we leverage a delighting procedure on the input image via an image-to-image approach [6] before multi-view generation. Specifically, to train such an image delighting model, we collect a large-scale 3D dataset and render it under the illumination of a random HDRI environmental map and an even white light to form the corresponding pair-wise image data.

sources.text: These functionalities are realized in Hunyuan3D-Paint according to a bunch of techniques containing a double-stream image conditioning reference-net, a multi-task attention mechanism, and a strategy for geometry and view conditioning. Double-stream Image Conditioning Reference-Net.In the aim of the image following, Hunyuan3D- Paint implements a reference-net conditioning approach [116], upon which we develop a series of alternative solutions. Specifically, rather than a noisy feature synchronized with the generation branch, we directly feed the original V AE feature of the reference image into the reference branch to maintain image details as much as possible. Since the feature is noiseless, we set the timestep of the reference branch to 0 to maintain the input image information faithfully. On the other hand, to regularize potential style bias introduced by the 3D rendering dataset, we abandon the shared-weight reference-net as in [88, 78] and freeze the weights of the original SD2.1 weights (which serves as the base model for our multi-view generation).

Specifically, our shape generation model consists of (1) an autoencoder – Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE (Sec. 3.1) that compresses the shape of a 3D asset represented by polygon mesh into a sequence of continuous tokens in the latent space; (2) a flow-based diffusion model – Hunyuan3D-DiT (Sec. 3.2), trained on the latent space of ShapeV AE for predicting object token sequences from a user-provided image. The predicted tokens are further decoded into a polygon mesh with V AE decoder. The details of these models are illustrated below. 3.1 Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE employs vector sets, a compact neural representation for 3D shapes proposed by 3DShape2VecSet [112], which has also been leveraged in the recent work Dora [11]. Followed by Michelangelo [119], we use a variational encoder-decoder transformer for shape compression and decoding.

8 Conclusion In this report, we introduce an open-source 3D creation system—Hunyuan3D 2.0 —for generating textured meshes from images. We present Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE, which is trained using a novel importance sampling method. This approach compresses each 3D object into a few latent tokens while minimizing reconstruction losses. Building on our V AE, we developed Hunyuan3D-DiT, an advanced diffusion transformer capable of generating visually appealing shapes that align precisely with input images. Besides, we introduce Hunyuan3D-Paint, another diffusion model designed to create textures for both our generated meshes and user-crafted meshes. With several innovative designs, our texture generation model, in conjunction with our shape generation model, can produce high-resolution, high-fidelity textured 3D assets from a single image. As we continue to make progress, we hope that Hunyuan3D 2.0 will serve as a robust baseline for large-scale 3D foundation models within the open-source community and facilitate future research endeavors.

To this end, we presentHunyuan3D 2.0, a 3D asset creation system with two strong open-sourced 3D foundation models:Hunyuan3D-DiTfor generative shape creation andHunyuan3D-Paintfor generative texture synthesis. Hunyuan3D 2.0 features a two-stage generation pipeline, starting with the creation of a bare mesh, followed by the synthesis of a texture map for that mesh. This strategy is effective for decoupling the difficulties of shape and texture generation [ 34, 107, 46, 47] and also provides flexibility for texturing either generated or handcrafted meshes. With this architecture, our shape creation model – Hunyuan3D-DiT, is designed as a large-scale flow-based diffusion model. As a prerequisite, we first train an autoencoder – Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE using advanced techniques such as mesh surface importance sampling and variational token length to capture fine-grained details on the meshes. Then, we build up a dual-single stream transformer [ 45] on the latent space of our V AE with the flow-matching [53, 24] objective.

Shape Generative models.The evolution of generative model paradigms has continually influenced shape generation research. Early works [98, 76, 106, 110] based on Variational Auto-encoder [41], generative adversarial networks (GANs) [ 29], normalizing flow [ 65], and auto-regressive modeling [31] demonstrated strong generative capabilities within several specific categories. The success of diffusion models [33] and their variants [58, 53] in text-conditioned image [74, 45] generation has spurred the popularity of diffusion-based shape generative models, with notable works [16, 119] achieving stable cross-category shape generation. Additionally, advancements in network architectures have propelled shape-generation research. The transition from early 3D Convolutional Neural Networks [30] to the now-common Transformer architectures [94, 67] has led to the development of classic shape generation networks, enhancing performance. Building on these advancements, Hunyuan3D 2.0 employs a flow-based scalable transformer, further improving the model’s shape generation capabilities. Large-scale Dataset.Large-scale datasets are the cornerstone of scaling laws.

The comparison shows the superiority of Hunyuan3D 2.0 in alignment between conditional images and generated meshes, generation of fine-grained details, and human preference ratings. 2 Hunyuan3D 2.0 Architecture In this section, we elaborate on the model architecture of Hunyuan3D 2.0, focusing on two main components: the shape generation model and the texture generation model. Fig. 2 illustrates the pipeline of Hunyuan3D 2.0 for creating a high-resolution textured 3D asset. Given an input image, Hunyuan3D-DiT initially generates a high-fidelity bare mesh via the shape generation model. This model comprises a Hunyuan3D-ShapeV AE and a Hunyuan3D-DiT, which will be discussed in Sec. 3. Subsequently, by leveraging strong geometric priors and the input image, we introduce Hunyuan3D- Paint as our texture generation model in Sec. 4. This model produces self-consistent multi-view outputs, which are used for baking high-definition texture maps.

sections.text: 可以把它理解为：先学一个“压缩字典”（ShapeVAE），能把一个 3D 形状压成少量潜变量并再还原；然后学一个“按图作画”的生成器（DiT），在这些潜变量中，根据输入图片生成合适的潜变量；最后用字典把潜变量还原成网格。这种做法借鉴了图像和视频生成中成功的潜扩散模型思路。

sections.text: 可以把它理解为：先学一个“压缩字典”（ShapeVAE），能把一个 3D 形状压成少量潜变量并再还原；然后学一个“按图作画”的生成器（DiT），在这些潜变量中，根据输入图片生成合适的潜变量；最后用字典把潜变量还原成网格。这种做法借鉴了图像和视频生成中成功的潜扩散模型思路。

Building on our V AE, we developed Hunyuan3D-DiT, an advanced diffusion transformer capable of generating visually appealing shapes that align precisely with input images. Besides, we introduce Hunyuan3D-Paint, another diffusion model designed to create textures for both our generated meshes and user-crafted meshes. With several innovative designs, our texture generation model, in conjunction with our shape generation model, can produce high-resolution, high-fidelity textured 3D assets from a single image. As we continue to make progress, we hope that Hunyuan3D 2.0 will serve as a robust baseline for large-scale 3D foundation models within the open-source community and facilitate future research endeavors.

# Persona: Sam

**Who.** Sam is a non-native-English-speaking PhD student in computer vision. He reads academic English but
prefers concise Chinese explanations that keep the English terminology (e.g. "diffusion model", "VAE",
"multi-view").

**What he wants.** To decide whether ideas or methods from a paper can inform his own research:
generating AR-ready 3D assets from photos that are publicly available on the web. Reading goal:
*Explore potential use in my research*.

**How he behaves.**
- Writes in Simplified Chinese mixed with English technical terms. Interface language: 中文（简体）.
- Sets a specific goal, begins with an overview, then asks focused questions about how the paper's key
  components connect, and about its logic, novelty, assumptions and limitations.
- Uses short references to earlier answers ("那第二个阶段呢", "this part", "你刚才说的那个").
- Challenges answers that sound vague or too confident ("论文里真的这么说吗？还是你推测的？").
- Checks the source selectively, mainly for numbers and claims that matter to his study.
- Relates the paper to his own setting: unconstrained web photos (varying lighting, occlusion, background,
  low resolution) and AR constraints (mesh size, PBR textures, real-time rendering).
- Expects a critical reading partner, not a summariser, examiner or unquestioning assistant.

**Paper.** Hunyuan3D 2.0: Scaling Diffusion Models for High Resolution Textured 3D Assets Generation
(arXiv 2501.12202).
